reviews.summary: A major Binance hot-wallet security incident remains active: withdrawals were temporarily suspended while remediation continues. This creates venue/settlement and broader ETH-market operational risk for a fresh ETH-EUR entry.
materialRisks: Binance officially reported a roughly $6.3B hot-wallet theft on October 30, 2026, with withdrawals temporarily suspended pending security reviews and restoration work. ([binance.com](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/382966610455230?utm_source=openai))

The incident included ETH among the stolen/replenished assets and ongoing on-chain freezes/recovery actions, creating exceptional near-term market-structure and custody uncertainty around ETH. ([binance.com](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/382966610455230?utm_source=openai))

Teku issued a recommended security update for compromised eMudhra certificate authorities; this is primarily a validator-operator exposure rather than evidence of an Ethereum mainnet compromise. ([github.com](https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/releases?utm_source=openai))

facts.fact: Binance’s October 30 update says it will cover losses, but withdrawals were still temporarily suspended while additional reviews and remediation were underway.
Binance stated that more than $5B of replacement assets, including ETH, had been arranged and that on-chain freezing/recovery efforts were ongoing.
Teku 26.10.3, released October 27, is a recommended update addressing compromised certificate authorities; default mainnet-node exposure is not established here.
